title: Parallel Sequencing of Barcoded BAC Clones by Random Tagging PCR
author: Elena Hilario
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.p3adqie
materials: Make a master mix according to the following table, with at least 16 extra reactions: This is a dense solution. Aliquot 17 µL of master mix per well with a multichannel pipette into its corresponding PCR plate. No need to add BSA, it has no effect on the amplification and it only adds to the cost. Platinum Pfx has been discontinued (April 2018) and replaced by another enzyme blend called Superfi (Invitrogen cat# 12351010). If you prefer to use another enzyme mix, just make sure is a proofreading type.

steps.title: Transfer BAC aliquots to working plate
steps.instruction: Using the robot’s 96‑pin HDRT, transfer an aliquot from each well of the 384‑well BAC glycerol stock plate into a 96‑well conical‑bottom working plate that already contains 150 µL LB medium with 12.5 µg/mL tetracycline; cover and incubate overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Defrost frozen BAC cultures
steps.instruction: Remove the BAC cell‑culture plates from the freezer and let the pellets thaw at room temperature for 10–20 min.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in buffer
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL resuspension buffer to each well, seal with packaging tape, vortex 10–20 s, then spin down briefly so that the bacterial pellet is completely dissolved.

steps.title: Lyse cells with lysis solution
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL lysis solution per well, gently swirl to mix, and incubate without shaking for 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Neutralize lysate with potassium acetate
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL ice‑cold potassium acetate solution per well, seal, vortex at the lowest speed with 3–4 pulses of 5 s each, and keep the plates on ice for 10 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate to pellet debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plates for 15 min at 3000 rpm at room temperature; most flocculent material will collect at the bottom of each well.

steps.title: Filter lysate through fritted plate
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a NUNC fritted plate assembled over a vacuum manifold with a corresponding 2 mL 96‑deep‑well receiving plate; cover with a silicone mat and apply –10 in Hg vacuum for 2 min (or until all liquid has passed). Discard the fritted plate.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: To each well of the receiving plate add 0.7 volumes (≈260 µL) isopropanol at room temperature, seal, vortex gently for 2–3 s three times, and incubate at room temperature for 1 h.

steps.title: Pellet DNA and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 25 min at room temperature, pour out the supernatant into a waste tray, keep the plate upside‑down and blot any remaining liquid with paper towels for 2–3 s, then dispose of the isopropanol waste according to local regulations.

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet with ethanol (first wash)
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL or 200 µL 70 % ethanol to each well, seal, swirl gently, let stand at room temperature for 10–20 min, then centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 25 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet with ethanol (second wash) and resuspend
steps.instruction: Pour out the ethanol supernatant, blot briefly, air‑dry the pellet ~10 min at room temperature, add 150 µL plasmid resuspension buffer (containing cresol red) per well, seal, spin down briefly, and store at 4 °C. The solution should appear red/pink (pH > 7.5). Optionally weigh the plate at 0, 5 and 10 min to monitor drying; if over‑dry, add buffer, vortex at medium speed and spin briefly. After sealing, let any remaining ethanol evaporate 10–20 min, then cover with lint‑free tissue paper.

steps.title: Inoculate fresh LB for plasmid amplification
steps.instruction: Transfer 20 µL from each well of the 96‑well working plate into the corresponding well of a 2 mL 96‑deep‑well plate containing 1.2 mL LB with 12.5 µg/mL tetracycline, seal with breathable tape, and incubate at 37 °C in a shaker at 180 rpm for 16 h. Plates may be stored at 4 °C for ~6 h or overnight before incubation to increase yield.

steps.title: Harvest bacterial cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the deep‑well plates at 3000 rpm for 25 min at room temperature, remove the breathable tape, invert the plates over a rectangular plastic box to pour out the medium, blot briefly, reseal with packaging tape, and store the plates at –20 °C until all plates are processed. Autoclave the discarded medium at 121 °C for 15 min before disposal. Use matching‑weight paper pieces under each plate for balanced handling.

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix
steps.instruction: Make a master mix according to the provided table (include at least 16 extra reactions), then aliquot 44 µL of master mix into each well of a PCR plate.

steps.title: Add t‑BACRB oligo and PEP‑PCR mix
steps.instruction: To each well add 1 µL of the appropriate t‑BACRB oligonucleotide and 2 µL of PEP‑PCR solution, seal with aluminium tape, vortex vigorously, and spin down briefly.

steps.title: Add BACRB oligo, plasmid DNA, and mineral oil
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL of the appropriate BACRB oligonucleotide and 5 µL of BAC plasmid solution to each well, seal, vortex, spin down, then add 20 µL sterile mineral oil with a multichannel pipette, seal with aluminium tape. Check wells for evaporation; if > 50 % of the reaction volume has evaporated, add 1X TE pH 7.5 buffer to bring the volume back to 50 µL and repeat the PEP‑PCR. Avoid contacting the well rim with oil.

steps.title: Run PEP‑PCR thermal program
steps.instruction: Thermal profile: 94 °C 2 min; then 50 cycles of 94 °C 40 s → 30 °C 2 min → 48 °C 4 min (ramp +0.1 °C/sec) → 68 °C 1 min; final 68 °C 7 min; hold at room temperature. Total run time ≈10 h.

steps.title: Run touchdown PCR program (optional)
steps.instruction: Thermal profile: 94 °C 2 min; 20 cycles of 94 °C 30 s → touchdown 68 °C→58 °C 30 s (decrease 0.5 °C per cycle) → 68 °C 1 min; then 10 cycles of 94 °C 30 s → 58 °C 30 s → 68 °C 1 min; final 68 °C 7 min; hold at room temperature.

steps.title: Store PCR plates before pooling
steps.instruction: For short‑term storage keep the PCR plates at 4 °C; for longer storage keep at –20 °C. The plates may contain 1 µL of 2 % xylene cyanole FF solution to visually confirm template addition before the next amplification round.

steps.title: Analyze PCR products on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Transfer the contents of each 96‑well plate (one quadrant) into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube (final volume ≈1.8 mL). Load 20 µL of each sample on a 2 % agarose gel in 1X TAE with a 1 kb+ ladder, run at 140 V (constant current) for 30 min, then stain with SybrSafe (3 µL in 50 mL 1X TAE) for 10 min.

steps.title: Pool quadrant DNA and precipitate
steps.instruction: Transfer 700 µL of each quadrant pool into a 15 mL conical tube (final volume ≈2.8 mL). Add 280 µL 3 M sodium acetate pH 5.2, vortex briefly, then add 1.96 mL isopropanol, vortex until mixed, and incubate at room temperature for 1 h.

steps.title: Ethanol wash of pooled DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 25 min, discard the isopropanol supernatant, add 1 mL 70 % ethanol, keep the pellet detached, incubate ~10 min at room temperature, then centrifuge again at 3000 rpm for 25 min.

steps.title: Dry pellet and resuspend in TE
steps.instruction: Remove the ethanol supernatant, blot the tube on paper towels without losing the pellet, air‑dry the pellet ~10 min, then add 300 µL TE buffer and store as needed.

steps.title: Run pooled DNA on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Load 2 µL of each pooled quadrant DNA onto a 2 % agarose gel in 1X TAE and run under standard conditions.

steps.title: Quantify and normalize BAC plasmid preps
steps.instruction: From each quadrant plate, select at least 12 BAC plasmid preps (48 total per library plate). Use 1 µL of each sample with the Qubit HS dsDNA kit, calculate the average concentration, and if necessary adjust each prep to ~3 ng/µL by adding more plasmid resuspension buffer.
